title: Reading moves
line: How a move is written: e4, Nf3, Bxc6, O-O, and what + and # mean.

steps.text: A move is written as the piece's letter, then the square it goes to. K is the king, Q the queen, R a rook, B a bishop and N a knight.
A pawn move has no letter: e4 means a pawn goes to e4. Play e4.
Play Nf3: a knight to f3.
Play Bb5: a bishop to b5.
steps.after: Black answered a6, attacking the bishop.

steps.text: An x means a capture: a piece moves onto an enemy piece and takes it off the board. Play Bxc6.
steps.after: Black answered dxc6. A pawn capture is written with the file the pawn came from.

steps.text: O-O is castling, a move of the king and a rook together, shown in a later lesson. Play O-O.
steps.hint: Move the king two squares to the right, to g1.
steps.after: The king went to g1 and the rook to f1. On the other side it is written O-O-O.

steps.text: A + means check, an attack on the king. A # means checkmate, which ends the game. Black's last move here was Qh4#.

summary: A move is the piece's letter and its square. An x is a capture, O-O is castling, + is check and # is checkmate.
